intro.label: Who we are
intro.text: Established in 2022, Live to Smile Foundation works in community mental health, education and human dignity. Through Hunger Free Kasaragod, we serve freshly cooked breakfasts and lunches, work toward a monthly target of 100 grocery kits, and rescue safe surplus food for neighbours across Kasaragod district.

rescue.label: Surplus Food Rescue
rescue.heading: Your celebration can feed a neighbourhood
rescue.sub: Weddings and birthdays often end with good food left over. We make sure it reaches people who need it, safely.
rescue.collectBody: Our team coordinates a prompt pickup using clean, food-grade containers. We accept only fresh, uncontaminated food prepared within the last two to three hours.
rescue.packBody: Volunteers check the food for freshness and hygiene, then pack safe portions for redistribution.
rescue.distributeBody: Safe rescued meals are delivered promptly to street dwellers and underserved neighbours.
rescue.name: Your name
rescue.whatsappNote: This opens WhatsApp with a draft message. Review the details and tap Send there; your request is not sent until you do.
rescue.context: Across Kasaragod district, wholesome food can remain after weddings, family celebrations, conventions, religious gatherings and hotel banquets while neighbours go hungry. Hunger Free Kasaragod connects event hosts, caterers and hotels with people who need a meal by coordinating the collection and dignified redistribution of safe surplus food.
rescue.quality: When surplus is identified, volunteers coordinate a pickup with the host and arrive with clean, food-grade containers. The team checks freshness, hygiene and handling, and accepts only uncontaminated food prepared within the previous two to three hours. Spoiled, stale or partially served food is never accepted. Safe meals are delivered to people in need within hours.
rescue.impact: Food Rescue provides an immediate meal while reducing avoidable food waste. Event hosts across Kasaragod, Kanhangad, Thrikkaripur and Cherkala can help turn untouched surplus into practical support for neighbours.

stories.label: Stories
stories.heading: People behind every plate
stories.pageIntro: Every meal served through Hunger Free Kasaragod carries a human story—of resilience, unseen struggle, and the simple power of showing up consistently.
stories.paragraphOne: When Live to Smile Foundation began its journey in September 2022 under the leadership of psychologist and social entrepreneur Ahammed Shareen, alongside Irfad Mayippadi and Abdul Rahman Erol, our work in community mental health and grassroots welfare brought us face-to-face with an uncomfortable truth: behind the bustling markets and bus stands of Kasaragod lived dozens of elderly citizens, stranded workers, and destitute individuals quietly enduring days without a proper meal.
stories.paragraphTwo: We realized that sporadic festive charity was not enough; hunger strikes every day, and relief had to be just as reliable. What started on 25 October 2025 as a humble once-a-week breakfast initiative soon revealed the true scale of need on our streets. As our volunteers walked the lanes of Kasaragod, Kanhangad, Thrikkaripur, and Cherkala, we met an abandoned senior citizen near the railway station who survived on tea for days, a recovering daily-wage worker unable to stand in queues, and families silently skipping dinner so their children could eat.
stories.paragraphThree: Those encounters transformed a weekly experiment into a six-day-a-week commitment. Today, the team serves 50 freshly cooked breakfasts and 80 lunches on each service day, alongside monthly dry-grocery kits and emergency food rescue. Supported by Kasaragod Municipality, Aster MIMS Foundation and The LaLiT Resort & Spa Bekal, the work is recorded in an open Distribution Ledger. Individual stories are shared only with permission, so the people we serve are represented with dignity.
stories.preview: We began by listening to people living with hunger on the streets of Kasaragod. Their experiences showed us that reliable, everyday support matters more than occasional charity.
stories.consentNote: Individual beneficiary stories and photographs are shared only when permission has been given and recorded.

impact.title: Impact rooted in daily action
impact.intro: Hunger is more than a physical ache; it erodes health, human dignity and social stability. Addressing last-mile nutritional gaps is a pressing local commitment and part of the wider goal of Zero Hunger.
impact.paragraphOne: At Live to Smile Foundation, impact is measured not only by the volume of meals served, but by the consistency and dignity with which support is delivered. Hunger Free Kasaragod works beyond fixed distribution centres, reaching people who may not be able to travel to them.
impact.paragraphTwo: On each of our six service days, we serve 50 freshly cooked breakfasts and 80 wholesome lunches—130 hot meals in total. We also work toward a monthly target of 100 dry-ration kits and rescue safe surplus food from events. Together, these three pathways offer practical food support to neighbours facing hardship.
impact.note: The 100-kit figure is a monthly target. Distribution totals are recorded separately in the public ledger.

ledgerPage.title: Distribution Ledger
ledgerPage.intro: An open, dated record of food distributions across Kasaragod district. Explore the entries, localities and totals behind our work.
ledgerPage.context: Transparency is the cornerstone of public trust at the Live to Smile Foundation. The Distribution Ledger is our open, living record of relief operations across Kasaragod district. Each entry records its date, project category—cooked food, dry-ration kits or surplus-food rescue—the quantity delivered and the locality served, including Kasaragod town, Theruvath Ubaid Park, Kanhangad, Thrikkaripur and Cherkala. From morning breakfasts and afternoon lunches to food rescued from a local event, distributions are recorded here. Browse the daily logs to see where support travelled and how grassroots logistics keep food moving across northern Kerala.
ledgerPage.empty: No distributions recorded yet. The first entries will appear here soon.

videos.label: Videos
videos.title: Videos from the field
videos.intro: A visual record of volunteers preparing meals, delivering grocery kits and rescuing surplus food across Kasaragod district.
videos.context: A single photograph often captures what statistics alone cannot—the quiet relief of a warm morning meal, the camaraderie of early-morning volunteers, and the shared humanity that binds a community together. The Hunger Free Kasaragod Gallery is a visual chronicle of our daily work across the streets, neighbourhoods and community kitchens of Kasaragod district. Here you can see volunteers preparing and packing breakfasts at dawn; morning distributions at Theruvath Ubaid Park; lunch rounds reaching daily-wage earners and street elders; families receiving monthly dry grocery kits; and food-rescue teams collecting untouched event food for people who need it. Every image is shared with respect for the dignity of those we serve, highlighting solidarity rather than pity.
